title: A Compliance Gap to Address
context: An internal audit reveals that employees never confirmed reading the data handling policy. Shortly after, a legal proceeding is opened on a customer file.

n1.text: Which evidence do you request first to demonstrate staff training?

choices.why: Attestations and acknowledgments are the expected evidence during an audit.

choices.text: A verbal statement from team leads
choices.why: A verbal statement is not traceable evidence.

choices.text: The page count of the policy
choices.why: Document length says nothing about its actual distribution.

n2.text: A legal proceeding begins: however, policy calls for deleting logs after 30 days. What do you decide?

choices.text: Place a legal hold and suspend automatic destruction
choices.why: A legal hold overrides standard retention and preserves evidence.
Destroying data relevant to a legal proceeding is a serious violation.

choices.text: Encrypt the logs and then delete them
choices.why: Encryption does not replace legally mandated retention.

n3.text: The regulator ultimately revokes the payment processing license. How do you classify this consequence?

choices.why: Revoking an operating authorization is precisely a loss of license.
Reputation is also affected, but the direct consequence is the loss of authorization.
There is a financial impact, but loss of license is more precise.

n4.outcome: You produced training evidence, preserved data under legal hold, and identified the loss of license.

debrief: Without attestations or acknowledgments, training remains unverifiable in an audit.
A legal hold suspends retention policy and overrides any automated deletion.
Revocation of an authorization is classified as loss of license, not merely a financial consequence.
